column3: The Hebrew calls the leaders heads of the fathers; BSB uses heads of the families.
The Hebrew repeats David as the subject preparing the place; BSB uses he.
The Hebrew uses an active setting verb for the altar and does not name Gibeon again. BSB states that the altar was in Gibeon.
The Hebrew separately narrates Solomon going up to the altar and offering burnt offerings; BSB begins with offering sacrifices.
The Hebrew asks what God should give; BSB renders a promise to give what Solomon asks.
The Hebrew says word rather than promise.
The Hebrew pictures going out and coming in before the people and asks who can judge them; BSB expresses leading and governing.
The Hebrew names the life of those who hate him; BSB expresses death for his enemies.
The Hebrew explicitly says from before the Tent of Meeting; BSB says before the Tent of Meeting.
The Hebrew first narrates gathering chariots and horsemen and then gives their numbers. BSB calls the second group horses and identifies the king as him.
The Hebrew explicitly says the merchants took them at a price; BSB expresses purchasing.
The Hebrew uses active bringing verbs and says silver without specifying shekels; BSB begins passively and supplies the unit. The final export clause explicitly mentions their hand.
